name: Primary Cutaneous Follicle Center Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of centrocytes and centroblasts forming follicle center cell proliferation in the dermis without epidermotropism
Expression of B-cell markers CD20+, CD79a+, BCL6+, and absence or weak expression of BCL2 in neoplastic cells
Solitary or grouped erythematous to violaceous plaques or nodules localized primarily on the head, neck, or trunk
Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement supporting B-cell clonality
No evidence of systemic lymphoma by imaging and bone marrow biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with immunophenotyping and clinical presentation consistent with primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma, excluding systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular data to differentiate from systemic follicular lymphoma with skin involvement.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary or grouped erythematous to violaceous cutaneous plaques or nodules

common.symptomName: Lesions localized on the scalp, forehead, or trunk
searchTerms: skin bumps on head or trunk

common.symptomName: Absence of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Slow progression over months to years

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
searchTerms: systemic signs like chills and losing weight

laboratory: Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing absence of systemic lymphadenopathy or organ involvement
genetic: Frequent t(14;18)(q32;q21) translocation absent or rare in PCFCL (distinguishing from systemic follicular lymphoma)
other: Histopathology showing follicular or diffuse proliferation of centrocytes and centroblasts in dermis
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a, BCL6; usually negative or weak BCL2

distinguishingFeatures: Typically presents with red to brown papules or plaques

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Grange F, Beylot-Barry M. Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma: a review. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2016;30(8):1309-1317.
